content.text:
There's no single magic number, but most guidance for school-age kids lands around **1–2 hours of recreational screen time on a typical day**, with a bit more flexibility on weekends — especially if the content is educational or you're watching something together.

What matters more than the clock:

- **What's getting crowded out.** If Kit's still moving, sleeping well, and connecting with people, that's a better signal than minutes logged.
- **Type of content.** Passive scrolling and fast-paced videos are harder on attention than a longer game or a show you've watched together.
- **Having a clear stopping point.** A set end time (not "just one more") prevents most of the friction.

The Child Development & Wellbeing framework flags that co-viewing and consistency matter more than a hard minute count at this age — so a weekend movie together counts very differently than two hours of solo YouTube.
